transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I came in because I just can't seem to shake this feeling that I've failed. I feel like I failed as a father, and... just as a useful person in general. It just keeps looping in my head, over and over, until I start to feel like I don't really deserve much of a future. That's mainly why I'm here.
Have you experienced periods like this before in your life, where you felt this way for an extended time, or is this the first time you're going through something like this?

No, not really. I mean, everyone has rough patches, but... nothing like this. This is the first time I've felt stuck like this for so long. Usually, bad days just pass, but I've never gone through anything quite like this before.
When did you first start feeling this way — can you remember approximately when these feelings of failure and hopelessness began?

I'd say it's been going on for about a month now. It started right around the time my daughter left for college. She went to a school out of state, and... well, ever since she moved out, I've just been feeling this way.
Over this past month, have you noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels?

Well, my sleep has definitely taken a hit. I just... I lie in bed for hours at night. The house is just too quiet now. And when I finally do fall asleep, I end up waking up around three or four in the morning. I can't get back to sleep after that because my mind just starts running through everything I've messed up. As for my appetite and energy, I haven't really been paying as much attention to those, but the sleep is definitely something I've noticed.
Besides feeling like you've failed, have you lost interest in things you normally enjoy doing, or do activities that used to bring you pleasure now feel pointless?

Yeah, I have. I used to really look forward to working on my model railway... and watching Cubs games with my daughter. But now, the trains just sit there half-built on the table. I haven't touched them at all. And even turning on a game on the TV just feels... pointless. I just don't have the desire to do any of it anymore.
Before your daughter left for college, were you already experiencing any of these feelings of worthlessness, failure, or hopelessness, or did they really only start after she moved away?

No, it really just started after she moved away. Like I said before, it's been about a month now, right when she left for that out-of-state school. Before that, I felt fine. But since she's been gone... yeah, that's when all this started.
Besides your daughter leaving for college, has anything else particularly stressful or upsetting happened to you in the past month or so?

No, not really. It's... it's just been her leaving. Everything else in my life is pretty much the same. There haven't been any other big changes or stressful events, just... just the house being empty now.
When you think about your daughter leaving for college, do you feel sad and miss her, or do you find yourself blaming yourself and feeling guilty in a way that seems different from just missing her?

It's... it's definitely different from just missing her. I mean, I do miss her, but that's actually why I came in to see you. I just can't shake this feeling that I failed. I feel like I failed as a father, and really, just as a useful person in general. 

It's not just normal sadness about her being gone. It's this guilt that just keeps looping in my head over and over. It loops so much that I honestly start to feel like I don't deserve much of a future.
When you mention not deserving much of a future, have you had any thoughts about harming yourself or ending your life?

Yeah. I have. It's... well, I've been having these thoughts that it would just be easier if I didn't wake up in the morning. And it actually scared me the other day. I caught myself going through all my finances, organizing everything... almost like I was getting things ready for someone else. That really shook me.

Have you experienced any beliefs or thoughts that feel absolutely true to you, but that others have told you don't make sense? Or have you heard voices or seen things that others around you couldn't hear or see?

No, nothing like that. I haven't heard any voices or seen things that aren't there. And I don't think I have any... any strange beliefs like you're describing. My thoughts are mostly just focused on what I told you—the guilt and feeling like a failure. But nothing that doesn't make sense or isn't real.

Over this past month, have you noticed that your movements or speech have felt slowed down, like everything is harder to do physically? Or on the flip side, have you felt restless or agitated, like you can't sit still?

I don't... I haven't really noticed anything like that. My speech and movements seem pretty normal to me. I'm not moving in slow motion or anything. And I haven't been pacing around or feeling restless, either. I mostly just sit there with my thoughts. So no, I wouldn't say there's been any physical change like you're describing.
